author: feature-implementer
summary: Fixed the owners listing pagination guard: GET /owners with a page value below 1 threw IllegalArgumentException from PageRequest.of(page - 1, size) and rendered the error page. processFindForm now clamps the requested page to a minimum of 1 before querying and before building the pagination model, so any page below 1 renders the first page with HTTP 200. Added OwnerControllerTests.processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage covering page=0 and page=-3, asserting HTTP 200, the owners/ownersList view, currentPage=1, and a repository query for page index 0.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Class sweep for the fixed pattern (an unvalidated `page` request parameter reaching `PageRequest.of(page - 1, size)`) found exactly one further instance in production code, outside this change set and unmodified by it: VetController.showVetList binds `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page` and passes it to `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` with no lower-bound clamp, so GET /vets.html?page=0 still throws IllegalArgumentException and renders the error page. Not blocking this slice: it is pre-existing behaviour on surface the diff does not touch, and the impact is an unhandled-exception error page rather than a disclosure or bypass (Spring Boot's default error view emits no stack trace). Raising it as a scope question, not a defect in this change: should REQ-OWN-002's clamp rule be stated as a listing-wide invariant covering the vets listing, or is it deliberately scoped to /owners?

approved_aspects: The untrusted `page` parameter is fully constrained before it reaches Spring Data: `Math.max(page, 1)` is computed once at the top of processFindForm and both downstream consumers (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) receive the clamped value, so no unclamped path to PageRequest.of survives in this method. Integer.MIN_VALUE is handled correctly by Math.max (no negation overflow), and a large page yields a valid empty Page rather than an arithmetic fault.

The fix removes an attacker-reachable unhandled-exception path (below-1 page previously produced the error page); replacing a 500 with a 200 narrows rather than widens the attack surface, and no new exception, error message, or debug detail is surfaced to the caller.

No injection surface introduced: `page` is bound as a primitive `int`, so non-numeric input is rejected by Spring's type conversion before any application code runs, and the clamped value reaches the database only as a Pageable through a Spring Data derived query -- consistent with the SQL-injection mitigation recorded in the system-design threat model.

No output-escaping regression: `currentPage` is now an int derived from a clamped int, and the pagination templates (owners/ownersList.html) consume it in Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions that require a String to be abusable; auto-escaping remains enabled and no `th:utext` or unescaped sink was added.

No secrets in the diff: the change set adds no literals, no configuration, and no credential-adjacent identifiers; a scan for token/password/secret/key-shaped values across both files returned nothing.

Supply chain unchanged: `scripts/changeset.sh --name-only` confirms build.gradle, the dependency lock surface, and all configuration files are untouched, so no new or upgraded dependency enters the build and no CVE re-analysis is warranted for this pass.
Test change is confined to src/test and adds no production-reachable code, no new endpoint, and no test-only bypass of validation.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The new test drives its two page values (0 and -3) through a `for` loop wrapping the mockMvc call and assertions. testing-principles.md § Assertions bars branching in assertion code ('No if/else, switch, or loops. Use collection-aware assertions instead') and the Agent Decision Checklist item 4 ('Linearity: No branching or loops in the test body?'). A loop over meaningfully-different inputs also hides which iteration fails: a failure reports 'expected 1 but was X' with no indication whether it was the page=0 or page=-3 case.
findings.fix: Convert to @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource (e.g. rows for page=0 and page=-3), each producing its own independently-reported test result, per testing-principles.md and the test-review checklist's 'Missing @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases' item.

findings.description: Test method name `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage` names the production method under test (processFindForm) rather than stating the behavior. testing-principles.md § Test Naming: 'The naming school is BDD: the{Subject}Should{Outcome} ... Applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward' — this is a newly-written test, so the school applies even though most of the surrounding suite predates it and is exempt.
findings.fix: Rename to a behavior-stated name, e.g. theOwnerSearchShouldShowFirstPageWhenRequestedPageIsBelowOne.

approved_aspects: Fix correctly clamps page to 1 for both page=0 and negative page values, and the reproducing test asserts HTTP 200, the currentPage model attribute, the rendered view, and (via argThat) the actual zero-based Pageable passed to the repository — a behavioral assertion, not just a status check
Mocking stays within the brief's policy: only MockMvc (the sanctioned HTTP-boundary double) and the repository's MockitoBean, consistent with the rest of the suite
No mystery literals: page values 0 and -3 are the meaningful (Tier 1) values under test and are self-explanatory in context
./gradlew test passes; no regression in the existing suite
